name: Target-level detection of respiratory pathogens against routine multiplex PCR, validation set (Sanderson et al. 2026)
description: Sensitivity and specificity of the sequencing workflow for each pathogen target tested by the routine PCR panel, in samples passing QC.

attributes.protocol: Each pathogen target tested by the sample's routine PCR assay is a gold-standard positive or negative; sequencing detection uses the configuration's criteria. Sensitivity = detected PCR-positive targets / PCR-positive targets; specificity = undetected PCR-negative targets / PCR-negative targets. Laboratory staff were blinded to validation results. 95% intervals are Clopper-Pearson where stated (Figure 6 legend).
attributes.source_locator: Methods 'Procedures' paragraphs 1 and 5; Results 'Validation Set: Diagnostic performance'
limitations: Only samples passing batch and internal QC (273 of 344) are scored.
Sensitivity is bounded by the PCR panel's targets; detections outside the panel are not scored.

Spectrum bias: inclusion required a pathogen detected at Ct or Cn 30 or below on the four-target assays, or FilmArray testing, with about one FilmArray-negative sample collected per eight positive samples; sensitivity and specificity are not estimates for unselected swabs.
Reads were mapped only to a curated database of the 23 PCR-panel pathogens, so the study does not measure detection of organisms outside the panel or false calls outside it.

name: sanderson2026 alternative sensitivity
description: Reported measurement transcribed from the pinned source. Not independently reproduced.

attributes.metric_qualifier: all PCR targets; target level; reference: routine multiplex PCR
attributes.source_locator: Results 'Validation Set: Diagnostic performance' paragraph 6: "increased sensitivity to 58% (95% CI 52-64%; 159/274)"
attributes.source_anomaly: The same sentence says the alternative criterion 'increased the number of samples passing batch controls from 260 to 274'; 260 is elsewhere the number of PCR-positive targets, not samples, and 159/260 is later reported as 61% for RNA pathogens only. The denominator's meaning needs a reviewer's judgement. Independent review 2026-10-11: 159/274 = 58.0% and 159/260 = 61.2% are each arithmetically consistent with the printed percentages; the 274 denominator appears to include the DNA targets that the 61% result excludes, and 'samples' in that sentence appears to mean targets. Kept as printed with this note.

name: Relevance of target-level detection against routine multiplex PCR, validation set (Sanderson et al. 2026) to "Select an RNA pathogen-detection workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: A prospective validation of one RNA metagenomic workflow on respiratory swabs, scored as target-level sensitivity and specificity against the original clinical PCR, with thresholds fixed on a separate derivation set, matches the use case's inputs (nuclease-treated respiratory RNA, reverse-transcribed) and its output (sensitivity against original clinical testing for one respiratory mNGS assay). It is proxy evidence for the same reason as the UCSF anchor: agreement with the clinical PCR panel is not sensitivity against all infections, and samples were selected by PCR result. It compares detection criteria within one workflow, not different workflows.

attributes.endpoint: Target-level sensitivity and specificity of a nanopore RNA metagenomic workflow against routine multiplex PCR in 344 prospectively collected nasopharyngeal swabs (273 passing QC), overall, by pathogen and by viral load, under pre-specified and post-hoc detection criteria
attributes.rationale: A prospective validation of one RNA metagenomic workflow on respiratory swabs, scored as target-level sensitivity and specificity against the original clinical PCR, with thresholds fixed on a separate derivation set, matches the use case's inputs (nuclease-treated respiratory RNA, reverse-transcribed) and its output (sensitivity against original clinical testing for one respiratory mNGS assay). It is proxy evidence for the same reason as the UCSF anchor: agreement with the clinical PCR panel is not sensitivity against all infections, and samples were selected by PCR result. It compares detection criteria within one workflow, not different workflows.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; specimens, reference assays and scoring units differ between sources.
Cite the pre-specified criteria as the validation result; the alternative criterion is post-hoc.
limitations: Preprint (medRxiv v2); the Journal of Infection version was not retrieved or compared.
The Abstract and Results give different specificity counts for the pre-specified criteria (3836/3845 against 3901/3910).
Upper respiratory swabs with high host background; sensitivity 51% overall, 19% for rhinovirus/enterovirus.
Nine false positives, attributed by the authors to barcode crossover in multiplexed runs.
71 of 344 samples failed QC and are not scored.
Tables 1 to 3 are images in the preprint and were not transcribed; only values printed in the text are recorded.

Spectrum bias: inclusion required a pathogen detected at Ct or Cn 30 or below on the four-target assays, or FilmArray testing, with about one FilmArray-negative sample collected per eight positive samples; sensitivity and specificity are not estimates for unselected swabs.
Reads were mapped only to a curated database of the 23 PCR-panel pathogens, so the study does not measure detection of organisms outside the panel or false calls outside it.
